description:
Create a signal: the account checks one thing on LinkedIn on a schedule and records every new item it finds as an event, which you read with get_signal_events. The first check records a silent baseline: what is already there is not reported, except that personPosts, companyPosts and postSearch signals report posts published since the signal was created. Creating a signal that already exists on the account (same type and target) returns that signal instead of a second one; a paused one stays paused. Pass only the target fields of the chosen type:
- network: no target. Reports connectionAccepted, connectionAdded and connectionRequestReceived. Checked every hour; spends nothing from account limits.
- profileViewers: no target. Reports profileViewed. Checked every 3 hours; spends nothing from account limits.
- personPosts: personUrl. companyPosts: companyUrl. Reports postPublished. Checked once or twice a day. The first check opens the profile or company page once (1 of stPersonProfileViews or stCompanyPageViews, and the person may see the account among their profile viewers); later checks mostly run as LinkedIn searches and spend some stSearchQueries – usually a few a day for the whole account – plus occasional visits.
- postSearch: term (1 to 3 phrases) and an optional filter. Reports postFound for new posts matching any phrase. Checked once or twice a day; each check spends 1 of stSearchQueries. By default an account has 300 searches a month and each postSearch signal spends 30 to 60 of them, so put the wordings of one topic into one signal rather than a signal per phrase.
- postEngagement: postUrl, or myPosts: true for the posts the account publishes. Reports commentAdded and reactionAdded. Spends nothing from account limits, apart from occasional visits. A postUrl signal watches the post for 30 days, then stops.
Fails with signalLimitReached when the account already has the maximum number of active signals of this type: pause or delete one first.

companyUrl.description: companyPosts only, required there. LinkedIn company page URL (e.g., 'https://www.linkedin.com/company/example').

filter.description: postSearch only, optional. Narrows the search; a post must match every field you set. The signal always looks for the newest posts, so there is no sort or date filter.

authorCompanies.description: Companies the author works at; matches any of them.

anyOf.description: Name of the person or company, shorthand for { name }.

id.description: Optional. URN or LinkedIn URL that pins the filter to exactly that person or company.

name.description: Required. Name of the person or company.

authorIndustries.description: Industries the author works in, by the names LinkedIn shows; matches any of them.

contentType.description: Kind of content the post must carry.

mentioningCompanies.description: Companies the post mentions; matches any of them.

anyOf.description: Name of the person or company, shorthand for { name }.

id.description: Optional. URN or LinkedIn URL that pins the filter to exactly that person or company.

name.description: Required. Name of the person or company.

mentioningMembers.description: People the post mentions; matches any of them. A name alone may match a namesake; an id pins the exact person.

anyOf.description: Name of the person or company, shorthand for { name }.

id.description: Optional. URN or LinkedIn URL that pins the filter to exactly that person or company.

name.description: Required. Name of the person or company.

postedBy.description: Author relationships to the account; matches any of them.

label.description: Optional. Your own identifier, up to 64 characters, such as a CRM record ID. It comes back with the signal and with every event it produces.

myPosts.description: postEngagement only. true to watch comments and reactions on the account's own posts. Pass postUrl or myPosts, not both.

personUrl.description: personPosts only, required there. LinkedIn profile URL of the person (e.g., 'https://www.linkedin.com/in/john-doe').

postUrl.description: postEngagement only. URL of the post whose new comments and reactions to report. Pass postUrl or myPosts, not both.

term.description: postSearch only, required there. 1 to 3 phrases, each up to 50 characters and with no quotation marks inside; a single phrase is a one-item array. Each phrase is searched as an exact phrase, and a post containing any of them is reported.

type.description: What to watch: network, profileViewers, personPosts, companyPosts, postSearch or postEngagement.

name: create_signal
